variables.reason: The ledger variable Ra is defined in the problem as the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations and uses the symbol 'Ra'. The KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness has canonical_quantity 'arithmetic mean roughness' with symbols Ra; R_a and definition 'Mean absolute deviation of surface height...' which precisely matches the problem meaning of Ra. That record explicitly lists si_dimension: L and si_unit: m, directly supporting the candidate exponent L=1 (length) while all other base exponents are zero. pq_mean_roughness_height corroborates the same dimensional classification (mean/area-averaged roughness height) and likewise has si_dimension L, so together these records justify the proposed SI vector.

The ledger variable kt is defined as the peak-to-valley height (vertical distance between highest peak and lowest valley). KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height uses symbols including kt and defines it as a roughness-amplitude measure formed from vertical height differences; it lists si_dimension: L and si_unit: m, directly supporting the candidate exponent L=1. pq_mean_roughness_height provides an additional corroborating entry classifying similar roughness heights as dimensional (length). These records apply to the kt named in the original problem because they share the same symbol and definition of peak-to-valley or maximum height difference.

The ledger variable k_rms is the root-mean-square height of surface fluctuations. KB record pq_rms_roughness_height has canonical_quantity 'root-mean-square roughness height' with symbols k_rms and defines it as 'Root-mean-square fluctuation of surface height about its mean.' The record declares si_dimension: L and si_unit: m, which directly supports the candidate exponent L=1 and all other exponents zero. This record applies because it names the same canonical quantity and symbol used in the problem statement.

The ledger variable Sk is the skewness of roughness height fluctuations. KB record pq_height_skewness has canonical_quantity 'surface-height skewness' with symbol Sk and definition 'Third standardized moment of the surface-height distribution.' It explicitly lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless), matching the candidate all-zero base exponents. This record applies because it identifies the same statistical moment (skewness) and symbol referenced in the original problem.

The ledger variable Ku is the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations. KB record pq_height_kurtosis has canonical_quantity 'surface-height kurtosis' with symbol Ku and definition 'Fourth standardized moment of the surface-height distribution.' It lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless), directly supporting the candidate all-zero SI exponents. The record applies to the problem variable because it names the same statistical standardized moment and symbol.

The ledger variable ES is the effective streamwise slope of the roughness. KB record pq_effective_surface_slope lists canonical_quantity 'effective surface slope' with symbols ES and aliases including 'streamwise effective slope' and defines it as 'Mean absolute gradient of surface height in a specified horizontal direction.' The record explicitly states si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless) because a gradient of length over length is dimensionless. This directly supports the candidate all-zero SI exponents and applies because it names the same symbol and physical definition as in the original problem.

The ledger variable Po is surface porosity. KB record pq_porosity has canonical_quantity 'porosity' with symbols Po and aliases 'void fraction' and defines it as 'Fraction of void or open volume/area...' The record lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless) and explicitly warns to confirm the geometric definition, but it supports the candidate all-zero SI exponents. This record applies because it provides the same symbol and the standard physical meaning of porosity used in the problem.
